# Jensen Huang resigns as Nvidia CEO after alleged affairs

Move follows admission of affair with woman alleged to be Chinese spy and reported relationships with two employees

- Nvidia crisis – live updates
 
- From washing dishes at Denny’s to rockstar of AI: the rise and fall of Jensen Huang
 

Dan Milmo and Dara Kerr

Thu 12 Nov 2026 17.05 ESTFirst published on Thu 12 Nov 2026 09.00 EST

Share

Prefer the Guardian on Google

Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive of Nvidia after reports of extramarital affairs with an alleged Chinese spy and two company employees.

He will be replaced on an interim basis by Nvidia’s chief financial officer, Colette Kress, until a full-time successor is named.

Shares in the chipmaker plunged by 13% when Wall Street opened, after Huang’s departure was announced. After a partial rebound, they closed down 4.3% on Thursday, wiping more than $180bn (£135bn) off Nvidia’s value on the day and around $490bn for the week – valuing the company at $4tn.

The statement from Nvidia’s board of directors confirming Huang’s departure did not mention the spying scandal and personal conduct revelations, instead paying tribute to Huang’s “profound” contributions to the company he co-founded.

“Jensen’s contributions to Nvidia are profound. Nvidia is one of the most consequential technology companies in the world. The board and the company thank Jensen for his immeasurable contributions to the company and the industry,” the statement said.

It added that Huang had resigned as chief executive, president and Nvidia board member “effective immediately”.

A graphic showing Nvidia’s share price fluctuating over time

Donald Trump, who had defended Huang at first as the scandal threatened to overwhelm the Nvidia co-founder, quickly moved on to potential successors on Thursday, posting on social media that he should be replaced by Tim Cook, Apple’s former chief executive and current executive chair.

“NOW THAT Nvidia CEO JENSEN HUANG, who has done a fantastic job, has resigned, there is only one man to take his place – TIM COOK of Apple,” Trump wrote, adding: “A Legend replaces a Legend!”

The chipmaker’s board earlier this week appointed the leading law firm Wachtell, Lipton, Rosen & Katz to conduct a “thorough and independent” investigation into the relationship with Alice Huang, an Nvidia customer and Chinese citizen who is no relation to the Nvidia boss. Nvidia had previously denied anything unusual about the relationship, but that changed on Sunday when Jensen Huang admitted he had been unfaithful to his wife, Lori, without referring to Alice Huang directly.

The law firm had directed Jensen Huang to continue to lead Nvidia as the investigation continued.

However, late on Wednesday, the New York Times reported that Huang had a separate extramarital affair with a company employee named Kimberly Powell. She was Nvidia’s vice-president of healthcare and was reportedly captured on video being affectionate with Huang at a hotel during a company conference in March.

The report added to the pressure on Huang, as the board called a meeting late on Wednesday to discuss the chief executive’s future.

Powell has been approached for comment.

After Huang’s resignation was announced on Thursday, Reuters reported a third alleged affair. The newly uncovered liaison was another Nvidia employee, according to two people familiar with the matter who spoke to the news outlet. Reuters did not reveal her name.

Nvidia’s board said it would consider internal and external candidates for the chief executive’s role, with Cook featuring among potential runners and riders before Trump’s intervention. Cook stepped down as chief executive at Apple in September but still has a senior executive role at the company. Rene Haas, the chief executive of Arm Holdings, a UK-based chipmaker, has also been mooted, along with Lisa Su, the chief executive of the chipmaker AMD.

Huang ran Nvidia tightly and managed about 60 direct reports. Internal candidates include Kress and Ian Buck, who manages the company’s AI hardware and software products. Huang’s two children, Madison and Spencer, also work at Nvidia but are in their mid-30s and relatively inexperienced. The chipmaker also announced the appointment of Harvey Jones, a tech investor and entrepreneur, as its first-ever chair.

Dan Ives, a senior US tech analyst, said the board had done what “it needed to do, which is rip off the Band-Aid and take Nvidia into its next chapter without him” and that the company remained ahead of its competitors.

However, Neil Wilson, an analyst at the investment platform Saxo UK, said Nvidia would need a “great CEO” to replace Huang.

“His technical knowledge and understanding of every last bit of product is basically unique and impossible to replicate,” Wilson said, adding nonetheless that Nvidia was well placed in terms of upcoming products and orders.

Huang’s exit from the company he co-founded in 1993 removes a senior figure in Silicon Valley at a time when the AI arms race between the US and China is at an apex. He owns more than 870m shares, or about 3.6% of the company, and was worth $145bn on Thursday morning, according to Bloomberg, making him the world’s 13th richest person.

Unlike many of his contemporaries at other leading tech companies, Huang has dozens of direct reports, an unusual management structure that emphasises his control over the company.

The entire AI ecosphere relies on Nvidia, which engineers advanced chips used to train AI models and power companies such as OpenAI and Anthropic. It is also one of the most valuable companies on Earth, with a market cap that hit $5tn at one point last year.

Huang has denied any knowledge that Alice Huang allegedly worked for the Chinese government. The pair were seen together around the world, dining in restaurants and attending meetings, over the past few years. Alice Huang is a businesswoman and head of the Singapore-based datacentre firm Megaspeed, who US intelligence services suspect of being a Chinese asset according to multiple reports.

On the same day that Jensen Huang admitted having an affair, Nvidia’s board of directors announced the company was launching an investigation regarding reports that he was the target of a foreign intelligence effort. Huang has agreed to testify before US Congress.

# A timeline of the affair scandal that sank Nvidia’s Jensen Huang

CEO behind the meteoric rise of Nvidia stepped down after it was revealed he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy

Johana Bhuiyan

Fri 13 Nov 2026 05.00 CETLast modified on Fri 13 Nov 2026 10.26 CET

Share

Prefer the Guardian on Google

Jensen Huang has stepped down as CEO of Nvidia, the company at the center of the AI boom, after leading it for more than 30 years.

Huang, an electrical engineer by education, stewarded the company from a $1bn firm when it went public in 1999 to a company valued at more than $4tn in 2026. But in a matter of days, after it was revealed he had an extramarital affair with a woman that US officials believe to be a Chinese spy, Huang managed to wipe more than $600bn from the company’s valuation.

Jensen Huang built an AI kingdom. Now he’s gone, will Nvidia’s ramparts be breached?

Read more

China has denied the accusations that it had tapped Alice Huang, the woman in question and a top executive at a datacenter company called Megaspeed, to be an intelligence asset, and called them a “smear”. US officials had reportedly started to monitor the Megaspeed executive after suspecting the firm was diverting powerful Nvidia AI chips to Chinese firms, in potential violation of export restrictions. The Biden and Trump administrations had prohibited US companies from exporting some of the more powerful AI chips to China over national security concerns.

Just a week ago it seemed that Huang’s ouster was unlikely, but in the days since he first disclosed an affair and affirmed his commitment to the company, the New York Times reported that there was a second affair – this time with another Nvidia executive.

A lot has happened in the last few days, but how did we get here? Here’s a timeline of what we know about Huang’s entanglements.

## 2023

### March 2023Megaspeed, a datacenter firm, is spun out from a Chinese video game company

Megaspeed is the datacenter firm at the center of the spy allegations. Before it was its own company, it was a part of one of China’s largest video game companies, 7Road Holdings Ltd. At this time, Megaspeed was controlled by a firm called Huang Le Ltd, an entity affiliated with Alice Huang, according to Bloomberg.

View image in fullscreen

The Megaspeed office in the Ocean Financial Centre in Singapore on 10 November 2026. Photograph: Taryn Ng/AFP/Getty Images

### November 2023Megaspeed is sold to a Singaporean shell company and becomes an Nvidia cloud partner

Huang Le Ltd sells its shares of Megaspeed to a Singaporean shell company called Swiftdata. The sale comes weeks after Joe Biden issued an executive order limiting investment in China’s AI industry.

Soon after, Megaspeed is designated an Nvidia cloud partner, which means the company could get preferential access to Nvidia’s advanced AI chips.

View image in fullscreen

Nvidia’s Jensen Huang speaks at the New York Times annual DealBook summit on 29 November 2023 in New York City. Photograph: Michael M Santiago/Getty Images

## 2024

### June 2024Alice Huang and Jensen Huang are seen together in Taipei, Taiwan

Jensen Huang is seen with Alice Huang at a bar in Taipei where several AI industry executives had gathered. The person who introduced them to each other was Alice Huang’s husband, Kang Wei, who had worked with her on several business ventures, according to the Wall Street Journal.

### 2024 to 2025Megaspeed receives several hundred shipments of Nvidia AI chips

The Singapore-based firm fields 200 shipments of AI chips, according to the New York Times. The company then rents out compute power, which is fueled by these AI chips, to major companies including the Chinese firms Tencent and Ali Baba.

View image in fullscreen

Workers unpack newly acquired Nvidia H100 chips at the Yotta Data Services Pvt datacenter in Navi Mumbai, India, on 14 March 2024. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

### September 2024The US Department of Commerce begins investigating Megaspeed

The commerce department begins investigating whether Megaspeed is diverting Nvidia chips to Chinese firms, according to the New York Times. This could violate export restrictions on advanced AI chips.

## 2025

### January 2025Jensen Huang meets Donald Trump for the first time

Huang visits Donald Trump in the weeks after he takes office.

View image in fullscreen

Donald Trump and Jensen Huang at the White House on 30 April 2025. Photograph: Ken Cedeno/UPI/Bloomberg via Getty Images

### April 2025Jensen Huang attends a dinner for donors at Mar-a-Lago

The dinner costs $1m a person and the president briefly puts a pause on imposing restrictions on Nvidia chip sales to China. The restriction is ultimately implemented shortly after.

### May 2025Jensen Huang is again seen with Alice Huang

The two attend an industry conference in Taiwan. The New York Times also reportes that Alice Huang visited the Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California, two months earlier.

View image in fullscreen

A screen grab from video footage shows Alice Huang attending a dinner with Jensen Huang at a restaurant in Taipei, Taiwan, on 22 May 2025. Photograph: CTI/Reuters

### October 2025Trump is reportedly briefed on the relationship between Alice Huang and Jensen Huang

The New York Times reports in October 2025 that intelligence officials told Trump that the two had a relationship and alleged that Alice Huang was a Chinese spy. Trump chose not to take action, according to the Times report. Trump has since said at a White House press conference that he didn’t remember being briefed on this.

### December 2025Trump approves the sale of more advanced Nvidia chips to China

Trump grants Nvidia permission to sell its second most powerful chips to China. A portion of the sales would go to the US government.

View image in fullscreen

Jensen Huang speaks to members of the media while arriving for a meeting with members of a Senate committee in Washington DC on 3 December 2025. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

## 2026

### May 2026Marco Rubio reportedly drafts a memo about Jensen Huang and Alice Huang

The US secretary of state, Marco Rubio, drafts the memo based on information gleaned from electronic surveillance of Alice Huang, according to the New York Times. The memo warns that Jensen Huang has become close to an alleged Chinese spy. Trump still invites Huang on his trip to China, saying in a social media post that he is honored to have “the Great Jensen Huang” on the trip.

### October 2026The New York Times reports Jensen Huang may have been targeted by a Chinese spy

At the time, Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo says Jensen Huang’s relationship with Alice Huang is nothing out of the ordinary.

### 8 November 2026Jensen Huang admits to having an affair

In a letter to employees, Huang says that he had an extramarital affair, apologizes to his family and reaffirms his commitment to the company. The Nvidia board says it is investigating the relationship but has no reason to believe national security secrets or company secrets were divulged. “The board has confidence in Jensen and his leadership team and will provide further updates as appropriate,” members of the Board say in a statement.

Silicon Valley leaders rally behind him, and at the time it appears that Huang might hang on to his job, despite his image being tarnished.

View image in fullscreen

The Nvidia headquarters in Santa Clara, California, on 12 November 2026. Photograph: Benjamin Fanjoy/Getty Images

### 9 November 2026Trump says he is ‘amazed’ by the allegations that Alice Huang is a spy

At a press conference, Trump says the FBI is investigating Jensen Huang but adds that he thinks Huang will be “in good shape”.

View image in fullscreen

Donald Trump at a news conference at the White House on 9 November 2026. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

“And I asked him about that, and he … said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy,” the president says at a press conference. “I asked him that question: ‘Did you have any idea that she was a spy?’ He said, ‘I had no idea that she was a spy.’”

“I really believe him,” Trump says.

### 10 November 2026A shareholder in California files a lawsuit against Nvidia and its CEO

Retail investor Mark Kistenmacher files a lawsuit accusing the company of misleading investors over Huang’s affair, claiming that Nvidia did not disclose the situation and raised national security concerns that could threaten the company’s business prospects.

### 11 November 2026The New York Times reports there was a second affair, and the Nvidia board reportedly prepares to oust Huang

The New York Times reports that Huang also allegedly had an affair with the company’s vice-president of healthcare.

View image in fullscreen

Jensen Huang at a reception in Tokyo, Japan, on 16 July 2026. Photograph: Bloomberg/Getty Images

At this point things are looking precarious for Jensen Huang, and then the Wall Street Journal reports that the Nvidia board is preparing to oust the CEO.

### 12 November 2026Jensen Huang steps down as CEO of Nvidia

Huang steps down, ending his 33-year tenure leading the company he co-founded in 1993. The board starts a search for the company’s next CEO while the company’s chief finance officer, Colette Kress, serves as interim CEO.

Meanwhile, shares in the company continue to plummet.

## Happening now: The Nvidia affair 
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has issued an apology to his family, the company and investors after admitting to an affair with a woman who is alleged to be a Chinese spy. 
The stock is under heavyselling pressure in premarket trading, currently down over 5% and lower by over 6% in Frankfurt.

Nvidia boss Jenson Huang has been embroiled in yet another cheating scandal, just days after the revelation that he had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy. 
In a message to Nvidia employees last week, Mr Huang admitted to being unfaithful to his wife and took "full responsibility" for his actions, while the company board revealed it had launched an investigation into the matter. 
Now, five people who have worked at the tech giant have come forward to the New York Times, alleging the billionaire had a second extramarital affair - with Nvidia's vice president of healthcare, Kimberly Powell, who reports to Mr Huang. 
Two sources claim the pair were spotted on video being affectionate in a San Jose hotel in March, where an Nvidia conference was going on at the time.

When contacted by the newspaper about a second alleged affair over the phone, Mr Huang reportedly said: "I don’t think you should be talking to me directly," and hung up.

Since Friday, Nvidia's stock has plummeted $500bn (£376bn), with shares falling eight per cent in after-hours trading on Wednesday alone following the news of another alleged infidelity.

Mr Huang has been asked to appear for a closed-door briefing with the House committee on his interactions with the alleged Chinese spy.

"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American." 
Donald Trump, when asked about the reports, said he had not spoken with the Nvidia chief about the allegations. 
He said: "I hope everything's fine. He's done such an incredible job." 
When pressed on whether he should have acted on intelligence when he was briefed on it, he added: "No, I don't think so. I think he's an honourable guy. I think he probably has an excuse for it. You have to hear it."
